newsitem.title: USA: Rorer sees Q4 hurt by product recall.
newsitem.headline: Rorer sees Q4 hurt by product recall.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said on Wednesday it expected its fourth quarter earnings to be hurt by a recall of blood plasma products by a joint-venture.

The company, 68-percent owned by France's Rhone-Poulenc SA, said its third quarter earnings per share were reduced $0.17 due to the effect of a voluntary recall of Albuminar and Plasma Plex by Centeon LLC, a joint venture with Hoechst AG.
It reported third quarter profits of $0.72 compared with pro forma earnings of $0.61 a year ago.

"The company's fourth quarter results will be impacted by lost sales of Centeon products, as Albuminar and Plasma Plex shipments are not expected to resume prior to January 1997," Rorer said in its statement with earnings.

The joint venture announced the recall earlier this month. At that time Rorer said the recall costs combined with potential lost sales could cut the consensus estimate for its 1996 earnings by 10 or 12 percent.
Estimates at that time stood at $3.56 a share for its 1996 earnings.
